E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (NZ transition & play-fast habits). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 2: *Hit The Tire Passing Game WIth No Goalie* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game*. One net: on a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the blue line (regroup) before attacking the same net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Use The Net)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 v 2 Dot Jumper. 2v2 race on a coach chip; each team's dot player is frozen until it gets a pass, then jumps in for a 3v2 on Liam's net. Tonight's constraint: the dot player must be used within 3 s of a possession change. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*? The race decides offense; offense attacks Liam. If the defenders win the puck they score by carrying it through a cone gate at the tops of the circles.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill* → Every rush goes into Liam's end; alternate start corners and send one 2-on-1 every ~20 s so he can set and track the late attacker. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie). Shot + rebound, then a D-to-D regroup that turns into a 2-on-1 back into Liam's same net (the step-up D must recover his gap). Theme rule: D-to-D must be on the tape at full speed; no stopping to settle. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)* → Cross-ice 3v3 to one net: the forecheck team attacks Liam; the retrieving team must skate behind Liam's net and then score by hitting a tire at the far end. The F1 pressure rule stays. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Rush shots need a lateral move or delay first (pre-shot movement) and no more than one rush every ~20 s.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.

  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks

Station 2 — sag|skills

  • Directions: Objective Ride The Bull is a small area game from Matt Thomas that works on developing puck protection and possession skills under pressure. Teams must protect the puck, use their teammates, and keep possession for 8 seconds.   • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-mjFcY9jvJg
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "3 v 2 Puck Protection Game." Official IHS 3v2 puck-protection game (Daniel Paille). Not Ride The Bull's 8-second possession then add a player; same protect-the-puck-under-pressure theme.

Station 3 — contact|systems

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.

  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Tursi, "Jets 2v2 drill." IHS 2v2 rush drill on YouTube (Jets 2v2). Not the Pioneer 1v1-to-2v2 progression; same 2v2 rush work.

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost.   • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2jPl1Ind8E0
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hockey Backcheck - Backchecking against a 2 on 1 and 3 on 2." Official IHS backcheck / tracking clip. Not Perry Pearn's 45-degree tracking game; run the written tracking-game rules.

Finisher (54–60): *ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)* → Cross-ice 3v3 to one net: the forecheck team attacks Liam; the retrieving team must skate behind Liam's net and then score by hitting a tire at the far end.   • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk

C. Small-area game (28–42)

USA Activation Drill (14U+)

  • Directions: Coach shoots a puck across; first two from each line race to it while the next two become activating D behind the nets. Possession side can attack or kick back to activating D for a 4v2. Run 30-second shifts; teach battle + activate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Bentley Wall Cycling Drill

  • Directions: This drill helps players work on their wall play and cycling under pressure. SETUP: This is a half ice drill, there should be a net in its usual spot on the goal line. There should be a line of players starting on one of the dots with a pile of pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jMDpyps_a3Q
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Half Ice Hockey Drill: Continuous Cycle Drill." Official IHS continuous cycle drill. Not Bentley Wall Cycling; same wall-cycle / cycle-under-pressure work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Compete night — SAGs & battles). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Liam's station — Station 1: *Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush*. One direction only, into Liam's end; the next pair leaves when Liam is set, and the D come back up the wall as their rest. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 2 (*Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)*) → no-goalie: Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies). Keep-away inside a faceoff circle (2v1 → 3v1 → 4v2 monkey-in-the-middle); no goalie needed. Keeps tonight's focus (Compete night — SAGs & battles) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 3 (*Ramsay 3 V 3 Race*) → no-goalie: 2vs2 Shooting Board Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 2v2 net-front game with shooting boards (no goalie); defenders stay goal-side, cut lanes, play the body. Keeps tonight's focus (Compete night — SAGs & battles) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • *Contact sprinkle (ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U))*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Tonight's constraint: ladder format — winners move up a court; 45-s shifts. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *USA Activation Drill (14U+)*? The possession side attacks Liam (or kicks it back to the activating D); if the other side wins it, they score by hitting a tire at the far dot after a D-to-D pass.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Bentley Wall Cycling Drill* → Already a one-net half-ice drill — keep it on Liam's net and alternate sides every rep so shots come from both walls. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters). Nets back-to-back in the slot, Liam covers BOTH; 2v2 or 3v3, each team must pass to its wall shooter before attacking. Theme rule: cap shifts at 30 s; coach whistles any puck under Liam's pads. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM* → Keep Liam's net live and put two tires on the far-end dots — the team attacking that way scores by hitting a tire. Flip ends at the halfway whistle. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Battles run long — cap shifts at 30–40 s and blow the whistle on any puck under Liam's pads.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. This drill can be used as a warm-up in practice or games, or as a drill to reinforce keeping your head up. Setup Setup 2, 3, or 4 players in the middle of a face-off circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Bentley Wall Cycling Drill

  • Directions: This drill helps players work on their wall play and cycling under pressure. SETUP: This is a half ice drill, there should be a net in its usual spot on the goal line. There should be a line of players starting on one of the dots with a pile of pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jMDpyps_a3Q
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Half Ice Hockey Drill: Continuous Cycle Drill." Official IHS continuous cycle drill. Not Bentley Wall Cycling; same wall-cycle / cycle-under-pressure work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Special-teams habits (PP entry / PK pressure)). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Side Middle Side* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Ride The Bull*) → no-goalie: The Gate Game (no goalie). 3v3, score by passing through one of three tire gates to a teammate; no net, no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Special-teams habits (PP entry / PK pressure)) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG*. The winner's exit shot goes on Liam; during his rest windows the exit shot goes at a tire in the empty net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Power Play Scoring Competition (Wes Wolfe). 60-s PP rounds on Liam: 5-on-0 entry, then one PKer added every 15 s up to 5-on-4; most goals wins. Tonight's constraint: entry must use the planned route (drop or kick-out); PK earns a point for every clear. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)*? Attack only toward Liam's net; when the backcheckers win the puck they 'score' by passing to their partners waiting in the small neutral zone.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free The Gate Game (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Bentley Wall Cycling Drill* → Already a one-net half-ice drill — keep it on Liam's net and alternate sides every rep so shots come from both walls. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Sticks In Lanes Game (Topher Scott). 6 fixed attackers vs 2 defenders in the middle, one net; 2+ passes through the middle before a shot; sticks on the ice. Theme rule: run it 6v3 (PP vs PK); 3 passes through the middle before a shot. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill* → The race and the 3v3 attack Liam's net; on a change of possession the new team must complete a pass to the coach at the blue line (that's the 'transition') before attacking the same net. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: PP one-timers only after 2+ passes; whistle after each goal or freeze so he resets.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Flip ends at the halfway whistle. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.

  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Oreo

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOLeLJdgGA
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "3v3 Continuous." Continuous 3v3 game. Not Lammers' Oreo (D must pass to the next players in line).

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill

  • Directions: Below-the-dots 3v3 rebound battle. Play off goalie rebounds and second chances; defense boxes out, offense crashes with sticks on ice. High-value for Liam’s rebound control.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEFVgm1aC4g
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill." Official IHS net-front / rebound battle. Not Holmstrom's 5-shot box SAG; same screen, tip, and rebound work.

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Middle-ice deny & stick detail). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Angle Behind Net + Stick Check* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*. The race and the 3v3 attack Liam's net; on a change of possession the new team must complete a pass to the coach at the blue line (that's the 'transition') before attacking the same net. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 3: *The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Gretzky 3 vs 2 Behind the Net. Below the circle tops, one net; team of 3 must always keep a forward below the goal line, D talk through the switches. Tonight's constraint: defenders get a point for any pass from behind the net they block with a stick. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Oreo* → Keep it on Liam's net (offense scores, defense outlets to the next line); cap shifts at 30 s so the shot count stays sane. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Sticks In Lanes Game (Topher Scott). 6 fixed attackers vs 2 defenders in the middle, one net; 2+ passes through the middle before a shot; sticks on the ice. Theme rule: run 6v3; the third defender guards the middle seam. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill* → Liam's net; one coach shot per rep and play the rebounds out; 25–30 s shifts with a two-second pause after every whistle so he can reset. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only through a lane the offense earned; no point blasts through a forest of sticks.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Perry Pearn Tracking Game

  • Directions: Objective The Perry Pearn Tracking Game from John Dean helps teams develop the habit of tracking through the puck at a 45-degree angle after possession is lost. The offensive team works together to prevent exits, extend zone time, and wear down defenders until pressure creates a turnover or scoring opportunity. 3 below an imaginary line connecting the tops of the circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2jPl1Ind8E0
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hockey Backcheck - Backchecking against a 2 on 1 and 3 on 2." Official IHS backcheck / tracking clip. Not Perry Pearn's 45-degree tracking game; run the written tracking-game rules.

All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.

Lay a spare net on its back against the standing net so only the top strip is open; shoot to the small target. Keeps tonight's focus (Scoring habits — catch & release) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • *Contact sprinkle (Perry Pearn Tracking Game)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.

  • Prefer to keep *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp*? One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam.

E. Finisher (54–60): *Back to Back Net Battle Hockey Game* → Liam covers BOTH back-to-back nets (Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters) format) — or turn one net toward the boards and count only shots that hit a tire set in its mouth.   • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

Buffalo 2v2 to 3v3 to 4v4

  • Directions: Objective A high tempo transition drill from Day 2 of the 2026 Buffalo Sabres Development Camp that Camp that starts as a 2v2 and progresses to a 3v3 and 4v4. Both teams are trying to defend & score. Setup Nets on goal line and blue line.

Keeps tonight's focus (Backcheck & recovery races) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video

  • *Contact sprinkle (1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position)* — no net needed; unchanged.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets). Cross-ice; one team shoots on Liam, the other scores by hitting 2 tires at the far end; flip ends every time the tire team scores. Tonight's constraint: when the tire team scores, its opponents must sprint-backcheck to the far blue line before re-entering. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • Prefer to keep *2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game*? Run as written on Liam's net, but the coach controls the feed: one shot, play the rebound out, new puck only when Liam is set. Cap at ~12 shots per rotation.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)* → Already a one-net game (offense shoots on Liam; defense scores by skating the puck between the tires) — run it exactly as written. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie). Shot + rebound, then a D-to-D regroup that turns into a 2-on-1 back into Liam's same net (the step-up D must recover his gap). Theme rule: the shooter from the first rush must backcheck through the middle on the 2-on-1. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Buffalo 2v2 to 3v3 to 4v4* → Liam stays in the goal-line net; the blue-line net is swapped for two tires (or a net turned to the boards) that count only off a pass from below the dots. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks

  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull the far-end net to the boards and set two tires on the goal line (tire targets). If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Pit Chaos Handling with Passes* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill*) → no-goalie: 1vs1 Three-Gate Game (IIHF Skills4Life). 1v1 in a faceoff circle; carry the puck out through any of three gates, roles flip on a turnover. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill*) → no-goalie: Transition Pivot Races. Head-to-head pivot race (forward–backward–forward) finishing in a race to a coach-placed puck; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (Controlled body contact & angling) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game*. Run as written on Liam's net, but the coach controls the feed: one shot, play the rebound out, new puck only when Liam is set. Cap at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets). Cross-ice; one team shoots on Liam, the other scores by hitting 2 tires at the far end; flip ends every time the tire team scores. Tonight's constraint: the tire team may only start its attack after winning the puck with an angle + stick (no lunging); illegal contact = possession to the other team. ▶ video (IHS page)

  • *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush* → One direction only, into Liam's end; the next pair leaves when Liam is set, and the D come back up the wall as their rest. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Theme rule: 45-s shifts; contact is controlled rub-outs only — count angle-and-pin wins. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!* → Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: No shot while a contact battle is still in the crease; pucks low and from the slot only, and Liam calls 'time' if bodies land on him.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

JJHC Varsity Practice — February 1, 2027

FieldValue
DateFebruary 1, 2027
Ice8:30 PM–9:30 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeSkating edges, gaps & retrievals
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires/pads, whistle

ADM split target: ~50% skills / 30% hockey sense (SAG) / 20% systems.

Board cue: Eyes up. Stick on ice. Move after every pass.

Goalie (Liam): Primary shot volume at Station 3 / scoring block. Call for catch-and-release quality.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–8A. Warm-up + puck flowSkills
8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Side Middle Side

  • Directions: The Side Middle Side passing drill from Darryl Belfry is from his practice plan, Parallel Teaching Structure - Passing Between Two Checks and One Touch Passing . This specific drill allows the whole team to warm up their skating, puck handling, passing and vision at the beginning of the practice. Setup Players line up at all 4 neutral zone face-off circles with pucks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeRHZLK2eek

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — skills|systems

Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill

  • Directions: 2-on-1 that uses the net as a pick/screen and deception tool. Offense delays, uses the net to change sides, and looks for the late attacker; defender manages gap and stick while protecting the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw

Station 2 — skills|contact

1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position

  • Directions: Skill clip on attack position for 1v1s—hands away, hip protection, attack the defender’s heels/hands. Use as a 30-second demo before 1v1 station work.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lexj0b5n7Ks

Station 3 — contact|warm-up

Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps. Contact every practice.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXQlcDUcGKE
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Tursi, "Jets 2v2 drill." IHS 2v2 rush drill on YouTube (Jets 2v2). Not the Pioneer 1v1-to-2v2 progression; same 2v2 rush work.

C. Small-area game (28–42)

The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game

  • Directions: Small-area give-and-go game inside a marked box. Score by connecting give-and-goes or hitting a target rule set by the coach. Cue pass-and-move immediately; sticks on ice for support.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcgkBs58qFk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game." Official IHS give-and-go small-area game. Not the NZ-only version; same give-and-go / move-after-the-pass habit.

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

Road Runner 3 v 2

  • Directions: Road Runner 3v2 Overview: Road Runner 3v2 is a high-tempo, continuous rush drill that reinforces key rush principles for both offense and defense. It challenges attackers to make quick decisions off the rush, encourages defenders to manage gaps and sort responsibilities, and teaches the importance of F3 tracking through the neutral zone to kill plays from above. Setup Coach starts with a puck near the top of the circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qGm4xRS8Rkk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Wally Kozak, "Leafs Continuous 3 on 2." Darryl Belfry continuous 3-on-2 rush. Not Road Runner 3v2; same high-tempo continuous 3v2 rush work.

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey

  • Directions: 3v1 keep-away to train support, deception, and defensive stick positioning. On turnover or after a time limit, flip roles. Progress to 3v2.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6epwQk1POE

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Skating edges, gaps & retrievals). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Side Middle Side* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Liam's station — Station 1: *Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill*. Every rush goes into Liam's end; alternate start corners and send one 2-on-1 every ~20 s so he can set and track the late attacker. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • Station 2: *1 on 1 Tips for Hockey Players: The Attack Position* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 3: *Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie). Net angled in the corner, dividers box the area; 2v2, 45-s shifts, keep score. Tonight's constraint: coach spots pucks into the corner — first player must win it with a protected retrieval (back to pressure) before a pass. ▶ video

  • *The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Transition Pivot Races; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *Road Runner 3 v 2* → Rushes go only into Liam's end; the return rush finishes with a pass through a cone gate at the far blue line instead of a shot. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Horseshoe Regroup 2-on-1 (one goalie). Shot + rebound, then a D-to-D regroup that turns into a 2-on-1 back into Liam's same net (the step-up D must recover his gap). Theme rule: forwards must make the regroup pass on their edges (C-cut, then pass) before the 2-on-1. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey* is goalie-free — run as written; Liam does 2 minutes of easy lateral movement and stretches in the crease.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots come in stride off the retrieval only — no stop-and-blast; one shot max per retrieval rep.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Shooting, rebounds & net-front). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: move the second net back-to-back with Liam's net in the slot for the SAG. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Liam's station — Station 2: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.

  • *Contact sprinkle (1 v 1 Puck Retrieval to 2 v 1)*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters). Nets back-to-back in the slot, Liam covers BOTH; 2v2 or 3v3, each team must pass to its wall shooter before attacking. Tonight's constraint: wall shooters shoot low for tips; Liam covers both nets so cap shifts at 30 s. ▶ video

  • *3 vs 1 Keep Away From Battery Hockey* is already goalie-free, so keeping it as written is fine; use the one-net game above when you want Liam in the SAG block.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Tomas Holmstrom SAG (net-front). Box from the dots to the circle tops; 3 O vs 2 D fight for net-front while a shooter fires 5 pucks (one per whistle); attackers tag up outside the box every whistle. Theme rule: shooter may delay for a screen; goals off tips/rebounds only. ▶ video (IHS page)

E. Finisher (54–60): *Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1* → Already low-volume on one net — keep it on Liam's net and finish each rep with one shot only. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.

  • Liam got quality game-like looks

Keeps tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Puck Race to Possession Game*. Race in the circle; on the second whistle the winner attacks Liam and the loser defends — the defender scores by carrying it out through a blue-line gate. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.

  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOLeLJdgGA
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "3v3 Continuous." Continuous 3v3 game. Not Lammers' Oreo (D must pass to the next players in line).

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!*: Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed. Liam: 0–5 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 5–8 Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset) with two shooters pulled from the warm-up — low shot, recover to feet, set on the next shooter.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1 (*Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush*) → no-goalie: Nowak No-Goalie Transition Game. 1v1 in the middle with wall support; carry it across outside the cones = 1 pt, through the middle gate = 2 pts; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Station 2 (*Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game*) → no-goalie: Transition Pivot Races. Head-to-head pivot race (forward–backward–forward) finishing in a race to a coach-placed puck; no goalie. Keeps tonight's focus (F1 forecheck & tracking) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill*. Two lines, alternate sides; one shot + one rebound per rep and the next shooter only goes when Liam is set (~15–20 s). Cap it at ~12 shots per rotation. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking))*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Tonight's constraint: when possession changes, the nearest forward is F1 and must pressure immediately while the puck is below the goal line. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *3 on 3 Add a D*? Keep Liam's net; replace the other net with two tires. The team going toward the tires must hit its activated D with a pass before it can score on a tire.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free Transition Pivot Races; swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *2 v 3 Entry Offense vs. Breakout Transition* → The entry attacks Liam; the breakout team 'scores' by completing the exit pass to a coach at the red line. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Theme rule: F1 angles the D toward the wall; F2 reads the outlet. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Oreo* → Keep it on Liam's net (offense scores, defense outlets to the next line); cap shifts at 30 s so the shot count stays sane. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 2 (≈15:00–16:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Shots only after a forecheck turnover, from below the tops of the circles — quality over volume.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg). Jeff Lerg: goalie warm-up first, SAGs after he's seen pucks, and game-like pre-shot movement over volume.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

drill_library.title: John Jay Varsity — Drill Library
drill_library.html:
John Jay Varsity — Drill Library

Built for Coachy 60-minute ADM practice plans. Each entry has a short written setup and a public YouTube video URL.

Where the drills webpage lives

  • Hub John Jay drill strip (6 IceHockeySystems Shorts): https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay
  • Private twin: https://franks-hub-private.pages.dev/#/johnjay
  • Config: `frank-hub/feeds.json` → `johnjay.videos` → IceHockeySystems
  • jjpuck.com Resources: menu exists but has no drill pages (empty). Club site is schedules/roster only.
  • Expanded sources: icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills, ADM Drill of the Month, USA Hockey articles.

Inventory: 38 drills with video links, plus 30 `one-goalie` additions (#39–68, added 2026-10-06), plus 5 focus additions (#69–73, added 2026-10-19). Machine-readable full scrape: `jj_drill_library.json` (54 entries).

Tags: `warm-up` | `skills` | `contact` | `sag` | `systems` | `goalie` | `one-goalie`

1. 1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

2. 2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward rule (e.g., clear/score after a takeaway). Offense must move to support; defense angles first, then stick, then body. Continuous short shifts so everyone gets reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

3. 1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

4. 3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

5. 2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

6. What it means to be a good leader with Gold Medalist Hayley Scamurra

  • Tags: `systems`
  • Directions: Team talk / leadership clip. Use as a 60–90 second board or locker-room cue on compete, accountability, and how leaders set the tone for practice and games. Not an on-ice drill—pair with a compete block the same night.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/wwOIUxHVMTw
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

7. New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Below-hash or half-zone boxes. Dump a puck; 1v1 then 2v2 with legal contact taught that night. Winner exits to a shot. Stop illegal hits immediately. Angle first, stick second, body third.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04EKvozxnmk
  • Video note: Corrected — the previous link was IceHockeySystems' "2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward" (same video as #2). This Evolution Hockey clip, "Small Area Battles 1v1 / 2v1 / 2v2," matches the 1v1-into-2v2 contact battle. oEmbed title verified.
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/trainingmaterials

8. 1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. The offensive team is trying to skate the puck through the gate while the defender is looking to strip the puck and score on net. Setup Setup a net and a gate as the goals.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xMDs6JiOsBE
  • Video note: YouTube of the same drill — IceHockeySystems_com, "Use the Net 1 v 1 Hockey Drill." Official IHS YouTube of the same drill.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/1-v-1-use-net

9. Angle Behind Net + Stick Check

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: O carries behind the net; X angles to force outside/into the corner and finishes with stick lift/press or controlled rub—no open-ice charge. Switch roles every few reps. Cue: stay slightly behind until the carrier clears the net, then close.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw

10. Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yUwNEdJtFAs
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "NHL Development Camp Race to Puck Game." Official IHS race-to-puck clip (Sabres camp 1v1 into a 2v1), not Elle Hartje's circle possession game. Same first action: win the puck race.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/puck-race-possession-game

11. Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Tags: `contact|systems`
  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXQlcDUcGKE
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Tursi, "Jets 2v2 drill." IHS 2v2 rush drill on YouTube (Jets 2v2). Not the Pioneer 1v1-to-2v2 progression; same 2v2 rush work.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pioneer-2-v-2-rush

12. Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Tags: `contact|warm-up`
  • Directions: Size-matched pairs. Side-by-side knees bent: 3 strides → shoulder/hip bump → continue; both directions. Lead with shoulder not head, elbows in, stick on ice. Half-speed first, then add a puck and board-side bumps. Contact every practice.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jai0vHhRuEY

13. Practice Goalie Shuffles & Edgework with No Crease

  • Tags: `goalie|skills`
  • Directions: Goalie edgework and shuffles that do not require a painted crease—use cones or boards. Pair with skater stations so Liam gets focused movement work while others rotate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EASYdYzvucU
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EASYdYzvucU

14. 2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|goalie|skills`
  • Directions: 2v2 battle off rebound looks. Coach or shooter creates a rebound; both pairs compete for second chances and net-front body position. Excellent goalie tracking volume.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtXlcBl3D2I

15. 3 on 3 Play Fast Small Area Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Classic IHS 3v3 play-fast SAG. Short shifts, continuous play, reward speed of support after a pass. Pair with the Hub Short of the same theme for a quick visual before the whistle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE

16. Corner Tires - Small Area Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Corner Tires is a small area game where the players score by hitting the tire with a puck. Set Up Place four tires on a rectangle as shown in the diagram. Make sure there is enough room from the tires to the edge so that there is room to play on all sides of the tires.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9LZa7cH-phw
  • Video note: YouTube substitution — IceHockeySystems_com, "Hit The Tire Passing Hockey Game WIth No Goalie." No YouTube of Corner Tires. Official IHS related game: score by hitting a tire, no goalie; tires on the face-off dots instead of four tires in a rectangle.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/corner-tires-small-area-game

17. Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: The Corner to Half Wall 2 vs 1 is an excellent small area game for all age levels that helps players practice a 2 vs 1 in a small space along the boards in the corner of the ice. The game reinforces important skills like keeping your head up, moving to open spaces, protecting the puck, and verbal & non-verbal communication. Offensive players should practice using the boards to make bank passes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hnLu_shT2J0
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/corner-half-wall-2-vs-1

18. Gates of Buffalo Small Area Passing Game

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: The major concept of the Gates of Buffalo Small Area Hockey Game is to practice moving to open space, communicating verbally and non-verbally with teammates, so they can score Goals by passing through Gates. This game framework will help players learn to play with their head up, communicate with teammates and move to open space. As a coach, If you commit to working on activities like this instead of memorization drills for a portion of each practice, you will marvel at how your team begins to work together.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlKKAFlVTLc
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/gates-buffalo-small-area-game

19. Hit The Tire Passing Game WIth No Goalie

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Hit The Tire Passing Game is a fun small area game that can be utilized when coaches want to work on passing and puck support concepts and/or there are no goalies available. Setup Place a tire on each of the face-off dots inside of a zone. The offensive team scores by hitting the tire in the opposite circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9LZa7cH-phw
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/hit-tire-passing-game-no-goalie

20. Ramsay 3 V 3 Race

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Jason Lammers describes the Ramsay 3 V 3 Race. This competitive small area game incorporates racing to the puck to determine which team is on offense. Setup Full ice setup with goalies in both nets.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2I8V86FKg10
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Evolution Hockey, "Small Area Game - In-Zone 3 v 3." In-zone 3v3 compete game. Not Ramsay's race-to-the-puck start; same 3v3 in-zone battle.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/ramsay-3-v-3-race

21. Swedish 2 vs 1 (Cross Ice)

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: This is a phenomenal drill in several ways. First, the concept of this drill can be used in many different areas of the ice. Secondly, it forces players to think 2 on 1's in tight spaces.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WXvZcoC_yxA
  • Video note: YouTube of the same drill — Tursi, "Swedish 2v1 crossice." Same IHS drill (Swedish 2 vs 1 Cross Ice) on YouTube.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/swedish-2-vs-1-cross-ice

22. Buffalo 2v2 to 3v3 to 4v4

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Objective A high tempo transition drill from Day 2 of the 2026 Buffalo Sabres Development Camp that Camp that starts as a 2v2 and progresses to a 3v3 and 4v4. Both teams are trying to defend & score. Setup Nets on goal line and blue line.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9shBF_rkkWw
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Hockey Drills/Situations, "2v2 Continuous 3v2." Continuous 2v2 that layers a 3v2. Not the full Buffalo 2v2→3v3→4v4 progression.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/buffalo-2v2-3v3-4v4-3

23. Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

24. Oreo

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Oreo 3 V 3 Game from Jason Lammers is a continuous game that is competitive in nature as it forces the defense to work to pass the puck to the next players in line, while the offensive team is trying to score. Setup In this example, 3 players line up on the blue line. The players behind them are on the opposite team.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FOLeLJdgGA
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "3v3 Continuous." Continuous 3v3 game. Not Lammers' Oreo (D must pass to the next players in line).
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/oreo

25. Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: Picket Fences is a great small area hockey game that can be setup as a 2 vs. The offensive team gets 2 points for scoring a goal and the defensive team gets 1 point by skating the puck between the tires . Setup: Teams are set up in one of the offensive zones in line with Dots.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sazqSJGB_Ek
  • Video note: YouTube of the same drill — Ben Eaves, "3 v 3 Picket Fence." Same drill: 3v3 two-tire game in the offensive zone.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/picket-fences

26. Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: The Sully 2 on 2 Transition Game from Michael Peca was recorded during the 2024-25 NHL Season. This is a high-tempo small-area game designed to develop quick transition skills, offensive movement, and defensive awareness. The drill encourages players to convert defense into offense efficiently while emphasizing strong defensive details and communication.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=526kbcfZPsk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Ben Eaves, "2v2 Continuous." Continuous 2v2. Not Peca's Sully transition game; same 2v2 transition/compete work.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/sully-2-on-2-transition-game

27. Shooting Off The Pass - Offensive Zone Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `skills|goalie`
  • Directions: Offensive-zone timing drill: receive in motion and shoot in one action. Emphasize catch-and-release, weight transfer, and getting the puck through from tough angles. Feed Liam quality looks.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eti1cwBR978

28. Use The Net 2 on 1 Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `skills|systems`
  • Directions: 2-on-1 that uses the net as a pick/screen and deception tool. Offense delays, uses the net to change sides, and looks for the late attacker; defender manages gap and stick while protecting the middle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e6ioQDMwYlw

29. Breakout Transition Game

  • Tags: `systems`
  • Directions: Objective: a 2 v 2 game were the offense is trying to score and the defense is working hard to create turnovers and breakout by passing the puck to their teammates at center ice. Setup: Set up nets across the zone. Draw a line down the middle of the ice from the blue line to end wall.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7NgjXy5otpY
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — Kristen Sagaert, "Zone Entry/Breakout 3v3 Game." 3v3 in-zone; defense must complete a breakout pass to teammates in the neutral zone, then those players attack. Close to the IHS breakout-transition game.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/breakout-transition-game

30. USA Activation Drill (14U+)

  • Tags: `systems|sag`
  • Directions: Coach shoots a puck across; first two from each line race to it while the next two become activating D behind the nets. Possession side can attack or kick back to activating D for a 4v2. Run 30-second shifts; teach battle + activate.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DK_N5S36_oE
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/news_article/show/716266-14u-usa-activation-drill

31. ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Tags: `systems|sag|contact`
  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbWV5UOkhlk
  • Video note: Corrected — the previous link was the Backcheck SAG (same video as #32). No official YouTube of the ADM drill exists (the ADM page is text and a diagram only). This Hockey Coach Vision clip, "Hockey Break Out Drills / Game 3v3," is a close equivalent: 3v3 cross-ice, and players must skate behind the net before attacking. Run the written F1-pressure rule on a turnover. oEmbed title verified.
  • Source page: https://www.admkids.com/news_article/show/754281-10u-18u-f1-forecheck-game

32. Backcheck Small Area Game (tracking)

  • Tags: `systems|sag|contact`
  • Directions: Two end zones and a small NZ. Attackers enter; once all four players are in the end zone, new defenders wait in NZ. Original attackers must backcheck as the other team attacks. Stress stops/starts and tracking all the way to the net.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

33. NZ Give and Go

  • Tags: `systems|skills`
  • Directions: Objective Develop off-puck movement and teach players to create give-and-go opportunities by moving immediately after a pass. The game encourages players to think ahead, recognize available space, and create new passing lanes to get the puck back. 2 game in the neutral zone .
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gcgkBs58qFk
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "The Box Game - Give & Go Small Area Hockey Game." Official IHS give-and-go small-area game. Not the NZ-only version; same give-and-go / move-after-the-pass habit.
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/nz-give-and-go-1

34. Chicago 5 Puck Warm-Up Hockey Drill For Full Team

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team warm-up with five pucks moving. Players keep circulating, exchanging passes, and filling lanes so the ice stays alive. Great openers for touch, awareness, and tempo before stations.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IsD9ZDgPO0k

35. Ice Hockey Passing Drill - Rondo Progressions

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: Rondo-style passing progressions (keep-away circles). Start with more attackers than defenders and shrink the outlet time. Cue one-touch options and body shape to receive.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JW2BBDdR07I
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JW2BBDdR07I

36. Pit Chaos Handling with Passes

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: The Pit Chaos Handling With Passing drill is an excellent activity that helps players work on awareness, puck handling, and passing skills. This drill can be used as a warm-up in practice or games, or as a drill to reinforce keeping your head up. Setup Setup 2, 3, or 4 players in the middle of a face-off circle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UxmQBKTJ2ss
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pit-chaos-handling-passes

37. Side Middle Side

  • Tags: `warm-up|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team passing warm-up from Darryl Belfry (IceHockeySystems; from his 1-touch passing / passing-between-two-checks practice). Players line up at all four neutral-zone face-off circles with pucks. Pattern: skate down the side, pass to the next player, and join that player's line; that player skates across the middle, passes, and joins the next line — side, middle, side. Don't catch a puck standing still; pass a little to the inside so the teammate can skate into it. Cue heads up: pass to where they're going, stay ready for the next puck, and don't leave the line too early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeRHZLK2eek

38. Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Tags: `warm-up|systems`

39. 2 vs 2 Game (With 1 Goalie & Tire Nets)

  • Tags: `sag|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Cross-ice game built for nights with one goalie: one team shoots on the goalie while the other team scores by hitting 1–3 tires set at the opposite end (more tires = easier). Coach flips a puck in on the whistle; change on a goal, a freeze, a puck out of play, or the whistle. Switch sides during the game (or every time the tire team scores) so everyone gets to attack the goalie. Scales to 2v2, 3v3 or 4v4.

40. Back to Back Nets – One Goalie (wall shooters)

  • Tags: `sag|one-goalie|goalie`
  • Directions: Nets back-to-back in the middle of the zone with ONE goalie covering both. Play 2v2 or 3v3; each team has a designated player on its offensive wall and must pass to that player to go on offense — the wall player can shoot or pass. A drawn line can keep defenders off the wall players. Designed for one-goalie practices and adds goalie skating/recovery reps (keep shifts short so it stays quality, not chaos).
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J66B2W1FF4E
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J66B2W1FF4E

41. 2v2 Tight Area in Corner (1 Goalie)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Place a net in the corner on an angle facing the slot and use boards/dividers to confine a small area that keeps pucks in. Play 2v2 in 45-second shifts and keep score. Only one net is live, so a single goalie handles it while the game teaches core offensive and defensive habits in tight space (support, protection, stick on puck, net-front).
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V97nywNK4lo
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V97nywNK4lo

42. Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey)

  • Tags: `sag|contact|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Draw a line across the corner about 6 ft behind the net; two players per team play 2v2 on a single net with a neutral goalie. Coach spots a loose puck to start a battle. On every change of possession the puck must be carried or passed below the goal line before the new team can attack. Coach defensive-side body position, stick on puck and awareness away from the puck; offensively, puck protection and support.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFqJT564ZgQ
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/smallareagames

43. 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Split one zone in half lengthwise; 3 forwards attack one net (one goalie) against 3 defenders. Coach chips the puck to the goalie, who directs it to the corner to start. Forwards earn 2 points for a goal; defenders earn 1 point by completing one pass and then exiting the zone. The rep ends on a goal, an exit, a goalie freeze or the whistle.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ynnmtmb-sLA (note: Video is The Hockey Think Tank's breakdown of the drill; scoring rules are from the IHS page.)

44. 3 on 2 Race to 5 (Cail MacLean)

  • Tags: `sag|systems|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Below the tops of the circles: 3 forwards vs 2 defensemen plus the goalie. Coach dumps a puck and the rep plays 10–20 seconds. Forwards get 1 point for a goal; defenders get 1 point for skating the puck past the line; the goalie's side gets 1 point for covering the puck. New players on every point; first to 5 wins.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ySPCjemXDpc

45. Tomas Holmstrom SAG (net-front)

  • Tags: `sag|goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Mark a box from just inside the dots/hash marks up to the tops of the circles. Three attackers vs two (or three) defenders battle inside it while a shooter at the top of the circles fires 5 pucks in a row — shots only (no direct passes), and only after the whistle. On each whistle attackers must tag up outside the box and re-win inside position for screens, tips and rebounds; defenders box out and block. Switch after 5 reps and keep score.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEFVgm1aC4g
  • Video note: YouTube equivalent — IceHockeySystems_com, "3 on 3 Down-Low Rebound Battle Drill." Official IHS net-front / rebound battle. Not Holmstrom's 5-shot box SAG; same screen, tip, and rebound work.
